lane: Escuelita primary design and outward intention
title: Space full in communities for the Zapatista little school
authors: Ejercito Zapatista de Liberacion Nacional; Subcomandante Insurgente Moises
evidence_scope: First-session capacity, host-family and Votan teaching structure, materials, and stated possibility of sending teachers elsewhere
sequence_assessment: community capacity was expanded from 500 to 1000 and then 1500 students
sequence_intervention: families, guardians, teachers, videos, textbooks, later remote materials, and possible invited teaching teams
sequence_review: the movement limited enrollment to housing and care capacity
sequence_later_outcome: establishes exposure design and outward intent, not alumni adoption or outcomes
disposition: F-198 search-frame context; no separate finding
notes: Primary movement statement. Intent is not evidence that later teaching teams or descendant institutions materialized.

title: L@s condiscipul@s V. L@s estudiant@s
authors: Ejercito Zapatista de Liberacion Nacional; Subcomandante Insurgente Marcos
evidence_scope: Invitation responses and first August 2013 community and CIDECI enrollment profile
sequence_assessment: about 3000 invitations, about 2500 affirmative replies, 1500 community students, and about 200 CIDECI students
sequence_intervention: large in-person and materials-based political education encounter
sequence_review: no public alumni registry or longitudinal follow-up is supplied
sequence_later_outcome: large exposure population; no adoption, project-formation, failure, or later-outcome denominator
disposition: F-198 search-frame context; no separate finding
notes: Use the official approximate counts as design context, not as a count of later sprouts.

title: Miembros de la UNAM apoyan a las bases de apoyo zapatistas agredidas
evidence_scope: Public solidarity action by university members including recent Escuelita alumni
sequence_allegation: reported aggression against Zapatista support bases
sequence_assessment: participants explicitly connect response to recent Escuelita coexistence
sequence_later_outcome: observable alumni action within months; no persistence or community outcome
notes: Strong for an alumni identity and action; not a representative alumni outcome.

title: Pronunciamiento de alumn@s de la Escuelita zapatista en agosto de 2013
authors: Ten August 2013 Escuelita alumni in Italy
evidence_scope: Named international alumni statement after the La Realidad attack
sequence_allegation: killing, injuries, and destruction reported at La Realidad
sequence_assessment: signers identify their shared August 2013 student experience
sequence_review: no organizational structure or follow-up review described
sequence_later_outcome: observable international alumni mobilization; no descendant institution or human outcome
notes: Named signers establish participation and joint action, not a stable organization.

title: Vendimia solidaria desde Colima en apoyo a la transportacion del CNI
authors: Escuelita alumni and Sixth Declaration adherents in Colima
access_status: complete officially reposted event notice inspected
evidence_scope: Fundraising event organized by alumni and allies for CNI travel
sequence_assessment: local organizers set a public fundraiser
sequence_intervention: food sale, exhibits, media, and cultural activities
sequence_review: no audited amount or later review reported
sequence_later_outcome: observable material solidarity; no evidence of organizational durability or participant outcomes
notes: One event demonstrates collective capacity but not institutional replication.

title: La Sexta llama a marchar: 11 meses de impunidad. Nos faltan 43
authors: Sixth Declaration collectives, organizations, individuals, and Escuelita alumni in the Valley of Mexico
evidence_scope: Escuelita alumni named among conveners of an Ayotzinapa march almost two years after the first session
sequence_assessment: collectives and alumni issue a public call
sequence_intervention: march and demands for truth, justice, and release of political prisoners
sequence_review: no participation denominator or later review
sequence_later_outcome: alumni category remained politically operative in 2015; no direct communal institution outcome
notes: Supports continuity beyond the immediate aftermath, not continuous identity of any one group.

title: Festival y Comparticion CompArte por la Humanidad sede alterna Grietas en el Muro
authors: Espacio de Coordinacion Grietas en el Muro and partner collectives
access_status: complete officially reposted event statement inspected
evidence_scope: Creation of an alternate CompArte site by collectives and individuals including Sixth Declaration adherents and Escuelita students
sequence_allegation: need for a local response to the EZLN CompArte call
sequence_assessment: mixed group of existing collectives, adherents, and alumni organized a Mexico City site
sequence_intervention: two-day festival, prior sharing session, workshops, arts, dialogue, and exchange
sequence_review: named coordination space and partner list provide an observable organizational node
sequence_later_outcome: post-Escuelita organization-level candidate with explicitly mixed lineage; later persistence requires separate records
notes: Does not say the Escuelita alone founded the coordination space or describe its internal governance.

title: Viaje colectivo a la Asamblea convocada por el CNI El Istmo es Nuestro
authors: Espacio de Coordinacion Grietas en el Muro; Mujeres y la Sexta; Red Movimiento y Corazon Zapatista
access_status: complete officially reposted event notice inspected
evidence_scope: Named Grietas en el Muro coordination role three years after the 2016 CompArte record
sequence_allegation: travel and coordination for a CNI assembly
sequence_review: no internal governance or membership continuity audit
disposition: F-195 persistence corroboration; no separate finding
notes: Activity persistence is not proof that the same people or practices persisted.

title: Diversos colectivos convocan al Mictlan Rebelde 2022
authors: Espacio de Coordinacion Grietas en el Muro and partner collectives
access_status: complete officially reposted event notice inspected
evidence_scope: Grietas en el Muro named as a convener of the eighteenth Mictlan Rebelde gathering
sequence_allegation: militarization and violence against Indigenous peoples
sequence_assessment: partner organizations issued a public call
sequence_intervention: political-cultural gathering, workshops, music, art, and memory work
disposition: F-195 persistence corroboration; no separate finding
notes: Supports durable public visibility of the coordination space, not residential or governance replication.

title: Pronunciamiento alto a la guerra contra los pueblos zapatistas
authors: Congreso Nacional Indigena and international and Mexican signatories
access_status: complete primary movement statement and organization list inspected
evidence_scope: Espacio de Coordinacion Grietas en el Muro appears as a named Mexican signatory in October 2024
sequence_allegation: violence and threats against Zapatista communities
sequence_assessment: CNI assembled a broad solidarity statement and signatory list
sequence_review: signatory presence only; no audit of activity or membership
sequence_later_outcome: confirms public organizational identity through at least October 2024
disposition: F-195 persistence corroboration; no separate finding
notes: A signature establishes current public identification, not continuous operations or outcomes.

title: On Community Building and the Zapatista Movement
publication: California Institute of Integral Studies podcast transcript
evidence_scope: Organizer reflection on five or six CIIS delegations between 2012 and 2018 and later encounters with former students
sequence_allegation: hierarchy, colonialism, and fragmented ways of living and learning
sequence_assessment: first-person retrospective observation, not a structured alumni study
sequence_intervention: Escuelita and other encounters; later care, organizing, political, and NGO work said to carry principles
sequence_review: former students were encountered at a later Albuquerque Zapatista encuentro
sequence_later_outcome: qualitative practice-transfer signal with bundled exposure and no named denominator or human outcomes
notes: The trips included several kinds of Zapatista encounter, so the effect cannot be assigned solely to the Escuelita.

title: Zapatista Seed Pedagogics: Beyond Rights, Creating a Decolonizing Co-education
publication: International Journal of Human Rights Education 7(1)
access_status: public abstract, author metadata, and methods description inspected; PDF endpoint returned 403 in this pass
evidence_scope: Qualitative transgeographic interviews with pro-Zapatista interlocutors involved in local social-change processes
sequence_allegation: oppressive power relations and colonial education
sequence_intervention: learning to learn and listen differently and mutual political-ethical education
sequence_review: reflexive and relational process rather than a fixed blueprint
sequence_later_outcome: supports outward learning and local process involvement but not Escuelita-specific project lineage or comparative outcomes
notes: Sympathetic interlocutors are not a representative alumni cohort.

title: Sowing Indigenous Autonomy: Building a Common Political-Ethical Territory of Struggle with Zapatista Seed Pedagogics
access_status: publisher abstract, methods summary, metadata, and references inspected
evidence_scope: Interviews with external activists in neo-Zapatista networks over three decades
sequence_allegation: internalized hierarchies, vanguards, historical erasure, and nation-state political identity
sequence_intervention: reflexive learning, ancestral memory, and organization of collectivities
sequence_review: life-long learning and transgeographic political-ethical subjectivity
sequence_later_outcome: reports collective organization beyond Chiapas without isolating the Escuelita or measuring durability and human outcomes
notes: A broader Zapatista diffusion study; it cannot identify an Escuelita treatment effect.

title: Locked Arms and Open Hearts for Ayotzinapa
access_status: complete public article and author note inspected
evidence_scope: Former Escuelita student's account of a small Okanagan Valley student solidarity mobilization
sequence_allegation: disappearance and killing of Ayotzinapa students
sequence_assessment: participants organized despite limited time, money, and institutional access
sequence_intervention: banners, photos, gatherings, and transnational solidarity
sequence_review: author note links participant identity to RAMA organizing
sequence_later_outcome: named path from Escuelita participation to later organizing activity; no causal or outcome evaluation
notes: The article does not say the Escuelita created RAMA or caused the action.

title: Food Sovereignty in Rebellion: Decolonization, Autonomy, Gender Equity and the Zapatista Solution
access_status: institutional repository metadata and indexed public reprint inspected
evidence_scope: Former student's later public analysis of Zapatista agroecology, education, autonomy, and gender equity
sequence_allegation: neoliberal food systems and colonial domination
sequence_intervention: public knowledge transmission and continuing organizing and editorial roles
sequence_review: author thanks the Zapatistas for accepting him into their school
sequence_later_outcome: continuing individual pathway; no alumni cohort, organizational adoption test, or later human outcome
notes: Useful as a traceable microcase, not proof of representative diffusion.

title: How Activists Take Zapatismo Home: South-to-North Dynamics in Transnational Social Movements
access_status: publisher abstract, metadata, and references inspected
evidence_scope: Ground-level implications of Northern activists adopting Zapatista tactics and reflexive politics before the Escuelita
sequence_allegation: economic and political domination and Northern activist privilege
sequence_intervention: local reflexivity and changes in activist focus
sequence_review: study also notes rifts with former allies and resource diversion from Chiapas
sequence_later_outcome: demonstrates outward Zapatista adaptation before 2013 and supplies an attribution control
notes: Post-2013 Zapatista resemblance cannot by itself establish Escuelita descent.

title: The Bridge Called Zapatismo: Transcultural and Transnational Activist Networks in Los Angeles and Beyond
access_status: publisher abstract and book description inspected
evidence_scope: Ethnographic study of Casa del Pueblo and Zapatista-inspired community organizations in Mexico City and Los Angeles before 2013
sequence_allegation: immigrant exclusion and one-way models of political diffusion
sequence_assessment: ethnographic research on transnational activist networks
sequence_intervention: community organizing of undocumented immigrants and local adaptation of Zapatista political culture
sequence_review: book emphasizes complex and problematic linkages, not simple copying
sequence_later_outcome: organizational Zapatista diffusion predates the Escuelita
notes: A genuine broader-Zapatista sprout that must not be recoded as an Escuelita result.

title: In Defense of Conviviality and the Collective Subject
access_status: open abstract, metadata, and indexed article summary inspected
evidence_scope: Universidad de la Tierra Califas described before the Escuelita as a project between network and collective pedagogy and as Zapatismo beyond Chiapas
sequence_assessment: political-theoretical essay grounded in local project practice
sequence_intervention: collective pedagogy, convivial tools, and community regeneration
sequence_review: no Escuelita exposure was possible because the publication predates it
sequence_later_outcome: preexisting Zapatista pedagogical ecosystem and direct attribution control
notes: Later Escuelita participants may have joined or strengthened the project, but the project itself is not an Escuelita seedling.
